questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was motivated by the opportunity to explore a new culture, meet new people, while expanding my knowledge of EU law

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any problems finding the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received e-mails containing the necessary information and the administration answered within reasonable time if I had any questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem for me, but I some of the other students had problems, so I would advise new students to start looking early in the process. I found my accommodation through Luiss.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it can get very expensive if you start looking late. You can join WhatsApp groups where people are looking for roommates. Some leasing agreements a mandatory rental period of 6 months.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to use a designated portal for class registration, which was a bit confusing at first, but it worked. It will always take some time to make sure the classes are not overlapping

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could send an e-mail to the administration, but I did not use it

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked fine. You could always re-register after the first week of classes if you wanted to switch.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for the classes you find the most interesting and go to the first week of classes and then you can re-register if you are not satisfied

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 4 of the courses I took (Data Protection, Innovation Law, Intellectual Property, European Criminal Law) the level of the lectures were at a good level and the professors were very skilled in their fields and for the most part at educating as well. However, the exams were very easy. International Economic Law in the first part of the course it was impossible to follow the lectures due to the English level of the professor and the exam was very difficult depending on who examined you.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly the same, there was little to no group work and some of the classes the final grade was based on among other factors attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Innovation Law & Regulation, European Criminal Law, Data Protection, Intellectual Property and International Economic Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Intellectual Property since Professor Geiger really made the course interesting and the exam form also was mostly relaxed.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Fitness was extremely expensive in the area I lived in (Parioli) and you also needed a medical certificate for 50 EUR

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going to restaurants was mostly very cheap and groceries were a bit more expensive than I had anticipated

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a football tournament that I participated in which was a good way to meet other people, padel tennis tournament and weekly socialising events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the sports events and I would recommend participating as much as possible in the introduction week since it is where most of the people meet their friends

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Participate in the ESN events, Porta Cortese on sunday is a great market, Sanctuary is a nice place to go on sunday for Erasmus students

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, had no issues with the culture at all. Only the more relaxed relationship with time

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to talk to people in class, they are usually very welcoming

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No issues

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people and the relaxed way of living and the food of course

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not stress about attending all classes. Prioritize going to as many events as possible and meet new people. Try to talk to people who are not from the same country as yourself, otherwise you might just only talk to people you could also talk to back home

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the ESN coordinators about any questions you might have, recommendations etc. They are very helpful and it is also an opportunity to get some local friends

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going outside of my comfort zone, talking to as many people as I had the energy for and gaining a lot of new friends all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any big challenges but at first it could be a bit intimidating being all alone in a new country, but that went away very quickly, since everyone is in the same boat

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
